- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

80
/


http://h:80/
1

=========================================================================
DEFINITIVE SPEC — cross-field-interactions (post-falsification)
Verified by ~21,000 executions: a 20,160-case byte-exact predictor grid
(0 mismatches on lines 1,4,7,8 and on idempotence), a 384-case is_valid
truth table (0 mismatches), 4 exhaustive 254-value byte scans, a ~50-case
port grammar sweep, and targeted argc/locale/newline/size probes.
=========================================================================

--- 0. PROGRAM ENTRY / ORDERING (strict three stages) ---
main(argc, argv):
  # STAGE 1 — arg count. Happens BEFORE anything else, including port parse.
  if argc - 1 < 6:                      # fewer than 6 positional args
      exit(1)                           # stdout: 0 bytes. stderr: 0 bytes. No message anywhere.
  # argv[7..] exist? silently ignored. Verified with 7, 8 and 507 total args.

  scheme_in   = argv[1]; host_in = argv[2]; port_in = argv[3]
  path_in     = argv[4]; query_in = argv[5]; frag_in = argv[6]
  # All are NUL-free byte strings (execve guarantees; NUL is unreachable).

  # STAGE 2 — port parse. May terminate the process. Nothing has been
  # printed or normalized yet, so stdout is guaranteed EMPTY on failure.
  port = parse_port(port_in)             # see section 1

  # STAGE 3 — normalize + print. Cannot fail.
  scheme = ascii_lower(scheme_in)        # section 2
  host   = host_in                       # verbatim, never touched
  path   = normalize_path(path_in)       # section 3
  query  = query_in                      # verbatim
  frag   = frag_in                       # verbatim

  print(scheme);          print(host);   print(itoa(port)); print(path)
  print(query);           print(frag)
  print(to_string(scheme, host, port, path, query, frag))   # section 4
  print(is_valid(host, path) ? "1" : "0")                   # section 5
  exit(0)
  # Exactly 8 lines, each terminated by one 0x0A (including the last).
  # Empty component -> empty line. stderr is 0 bytes on success.

--- 1. parse_port(s) -> i32 ---
# Grammar is exactly strtol/stoi base-10 PREFIX syntax:
#   [ WS* ] [ '+' | '-' ] DIGIT+        WS = {' ','\t','\n','\v','\f','\r'}
#   DIGIT = ASCII '0'..'9' ONLY (Arabic-Indic '٣' and fullwidth '２' are NOT digits)
# At most ONE sign, and whitespace may precede the sign but NEVER follow it.
# Parsing stops at the first non-digit; the remainder is discarded silently.
fn parse_port(s):
    (v, ok, overflow) = strtol_i32_prefix(s)
    if not ok:        ABORT_INVALID_ARGUMENT()   # no digits found after optional WS+sign
    if overflow:      ABORT_OUT_OF_RANGE()       # value outside i32 range
    if v < 0 or v > 65535: return -1             # CLAMP to the sentinel
    return v

ABORT_INVALID_ARGUMENT(): stdout=0 bytes; exit code 134 (SIGABRT, core dumped);
  stderr exactly:
      terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
        what():  stoi
ABORT_OUT_OF_RANGE():     stdout=0 bytes; exit code 134; stderr exactly:
      terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range'
        what():  stoi

# Accept table (all observed):
#  "80"->80  " 80"->80  "  80"->80  "\t80"->80  "\n80"->80  "80\n"->80
#  "+80"->80 "+0"->0   "-0"->0     "-00"->0    "007"->7    "0080"->80
#  "80 "->80 "80abc"->80 "80.5"->80 "1_000"->1 "0x50"->0   "0X50"->0
#  "0b11"->0 "1e3"->1  "65535."->65535 " +65535 "->65535
#  "8\n0"->8  "80\n90"->80   " -1"->-1  "-1 "->-1
# Clamp table: -2->-1  -1->-1  -0->0  0->0  1->1  65534->65534
#  65535->65535  65536->-1  65537->-1  100000->-1  65536abc->-1
#  6553599->-1  +65536->-1  2147483646->-1  2147483647->-1  -2147483648->-1
# invalid_argument: "" " " "\t" "\n" "+" "-" "." "abc" "NaN" "inf" "INF"
#                   "e5" "++80" "--80" "+ 80" "- 80" "٣" "２"
# out_of_range:     "2147483648" "99999999999999999999" "-2147483649"
# NOTE: EMPTY port string ABORTS. There is no default port.
# NOTE: the clamp is observationally identical whether written as
#   (v<0||v>65535) or as an unsigned range test; either is correct.

--- 2. ascii_lower(s) — applies to SCHEME ONLY ---
for each byte b: if 0x41 <= b <= 0x5A { b += 0x20 }   # else unchanged
# EXHAUSTIVE: bytes 1..255 scanned; ONLY 0x41..0x5A change. No trimming,
# no validation, no filtering, no length rule, no non-ASCII case folding.
# LOCALE-INDEPENDENT (C, C.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8, tr_TR.UTF-8,
# en_US.ISO-8859-1, POSIX, invalid all identical). Use ASCII arithmetic,
# NOT a locale-aware tolower.
#   "HTTP"->"http"  " HTTP "->" http "  "HTTP:"->"http:"
#   "HTTP://"->"http://"  "1HTTP"->"1http"  "A-B_C+D.E~F"->"a-b_c+d.e~f"
#   "ÄÖÜI"->"ÄÖÜi" (bytes c3 84 c3 96 c3 9c 69)
# HOST, QUERY, FRAGMENT are NEVER case-folded (254-byte scans: 0 changes).

--- 3. normalize_path(p) ---
if p.is_empty():        return ""             # empty stays empty
if p.as_bytes()[0] == 0x2F ('/'): return p    # unchanged
return "/" + p                                # prepend exactly one '/'
# EXHAUSTIVE over all 254 testable first bytes. This is the ONLY structural
# mutation in the whole program. NO dot-segment collapsing, NO '//'
# collapsing, NO trimming, NO percent re-coding, NO backslash conversion.
# Independent of scheme/host/port/query/fragment.
#  "a"->"/a"  " "->"/ "  "\t"->"/\t"  "\\a"->"/\\a"  "."->"/."  ".."->"/.."
#  "?"->"/?"  "#"->"/#"  "?#"->"/?#"  "?q"->"/?q"  "%2F"->"/%2F"
#  "./a/../b"->"/./a/../b"   "a/../../../../etc/passwd" -> "/a/../../../../etc/passwd"
#  "/"->"/"  "//"->"//"  "///"->"///"  "//evil.com/x"->"//evil.com/x"

--- 4. to_string() — PURE CONCATENATION, NO RE-PARSING ---
fn to_string(scheme, host, port, path, query, frag) -> String:
    s = ""
    if !scheme.is_empty():               # <-- the ONLY gate on the authority
        s += scheme
        s += "://"                       # UNCONDITIONAL after a non-empty scheme
        s += host                        # even if empty
        if port >= 0:                    # 0 IS emitted; -1 is not
            s += ":" + itoa(port)
    s += path                            # normalized path
    if !query.is_empty(): s += "?" + query
    if !frag.is_empty():  s += "#" + frag
    return s

# CROSS-FIELD LAWS (each independently verified):
# L1. scheme.is_empty() erases the ENTIRE authority — host AND ":"+port —
#     even though host() and port() still report them.
#       ("","hh","80","","","")     -> line2="hh" line3="80" line7=""   (EMPTY!)
#       ("","hh","65535","","","")  -> line7=""
#       ("","","80","/p","","")     -> line7="/p"
#       ("","","0","/p","q","f")    -> line7="/p?q#f"
#       ("","hh","-1","//evil.com/x","","") -> line7="//evil.com/x"
# L2. A non-empty scheme ALWAYS yields "://", even with empty host and port<0.
#       ("http","","-1","","","")    -> line7="http://"        line8=0
#       ("http","","-1","/p","","")  -> line7="http:///p"      line8=1
#       ("http","","-1","","","f")   -> line7="http://#f"      line8=0
#       ("http","","-1","","q","")   -> line7="http://?q"      line8=0
#       ("file","","-1","/etc/hosts","","") -> line7="file:///etc/hosts"
#     Any non-empty scheme qualifies, however absurd:
#       (" ","hh","80","/p","","")   -> line7=" ://hh:80/p"
#       (":","hh","80","/p","","")   -> line7=":://hh:80/p"
#       ("//","hh","80","/p","","")  -> line7="//://hh:80/p"
#       ("http://h:80/p?q#f","","-1","","","") -> line7="http://h:80/p?q#f://"
# L3. ":"+port is emitted with an EMPTY host, giving a bare-colon authority:
#       ("http","","80","","","")    -> line7="http://:80"     line8=0
#       ("http","","0","","","")     -> line7="http://:0"      line8=0
#       ("http","","0","/p","","")   -> line7="http://:0/p"    line8=1
#       ("http","","80","a","","")   -> line4="/a" line7="http://:80/a"
# L4. HOST is an opaque byte string. ':'+digits, userinfo, '/', '?', '#'
#     are NEVER split out and NEVER override argv[3]:
#       ("http","h:9090","80","/","","")  -> line7="http://h:9090:80/"
#       (":80","8080")                    -> line7="http://:80:8080/"
#       ("h:","80")                       -> line7="http://h::80/"
#       ("h:99999","80")                  -> line7="http://h:99999:80/"
#       ("[::1]","8080")                  -> line7="http://[::1]:8080/"
#       ("u:p@h","80")                    -> line7="http://u:p@h:80/"
#       ("@","80")->"http://@:80/"  ("u@",-1)->"http://u@"  ("@h",-1)->"http://@h"
#       ("h/x","80","/y")                 -> line7="http://h/x:80/y"
#       ("h?q","80","/y","z")             -> line7="http://h?q:80/y?z"
#       ("h#f","80","/y","","g")          -> line7="http://h#f:80/y#g"
#       ("h//x","80","")                  -> line7="http://h//x:80"

#     are set), so to_string() is ambiguous:
#       ("http","h","80","/p?x=1#f","","") -> 4="/p?x=1#f" 5="" 6=""
#                                            7="http://h:80/p?x=1#f"

#       ("http","h","80","/","","?x")   -> 7="http://h:80/#?x"

#       ("http","h","80","/"," "," ")   -> 7="http://h:80/? # "

#       ("","","-1","","q","")          -> 7="?q"
#       ("","","-1","","","f")          -> 7="#f"
#       ("","","-1","","q","f")         -> 7="?q#f"

--- 5. is_valid() ---
fn is_valid(host, path) -> bool:  return !host.is_empty() || !path.is_empty()

# (scheme{"",http,file," "} x host{"","h"," "} x path{"","/p","p"," "} x

#   ("http","","0","","","")    -> 0   (though line7="http://:0")
#   ("http","","80","","q","f") -> 0   (though line7="http://:80?q#f")

# DECOUPLING (do NOT conflate with to_string emptiness):
#   valid + empty string:   ("","hh","-1","","","")  -> 7=""        8=1

#   ("http","h","80","/p?x=1#f","","")  ==  ("http","h","80","/p","x=1","f")

#   ("http","h:9090","-1","/x","","")   ==  ("http","h","9090","/x","","")
#        both -> "http://h:9090/x"
#   ("http","/p","-1","","","")         ==  ("http","","-1","/p","","")
#        both -> "http:///p"            (host/path swap collides)
#   ("http","h","-1","/x?y","","")      ==  ("http","h","-1","/x","y","")
#        both -> "http://h/x?y"

#   ("","hh","-1","","","") -> 7="" 8=1   vs   ("","","-1","","","") -> 7="" 8=0
# There is no from_string()/parse() entry point on this CLI; all 6 args are
# components. Never attempt to recover components from line 7.

--- 7. IDEMPOTENCE ---
# normalize is a true fixed point on VALUES: re-feeding the six component
# values reproduces byte-identical output (20,160/20,160 cases).
# ascii_lower, the '/'-prepend and the port clamp are each idempotent;
# junk ports converge in one pass ("80abc"->80->80; "70000"->-1->-1).

# scheme/host/path/query/fragment contains 0x0A, stdout has MORE than 8
# lines and lines 1-6 no longer equal the components:
#   ("http", "a\nb", "80", "/p", "", "") -> 10 lines:
#     http | a | b | 80 | /p |  |  | http://a | b:80/p | 1
#   Re-feeding those lines makes argv[3]="b" -> exit 134 std::invalid_argument.
# CR (0x0D) is retained without shifting lines: host="a\rb" ->
#   line2="a\rb", line7="http://a\rb:80/".
# A newline inside PORT never shifts lines (port becomes an int).

--- 8. SIZE / EXIT-CODE SUMMARY ---
# No in-process length limit or truncation:
#   5000 bytes/field, scheme uppercase, port 80 ->
#     lens 5000,5000,2,5001,5000,5000,25009,1 ; exit 0
#   100000 bytes/field, scheme "http" -> line7 = 400013 bytes; exit 0; valid 1
#   (both exactly equal the section-4 formula)
# External boundary only: ~900000 bytes x 2 fields -> execve E2BIG
#   ("Argument list too long"); the program never runs. Not the program's
#   behavior; a reimplementation need not reproduce it.
# Exit codes:  0 = success (8 lines)
#              1 = fewer than 6 positional args (0 stdout, 0 stderr)
#            134 = SIGABRT from the port parse (0 stdout, stderr diagnostic)
